newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH IPB SAYS NOMURA TALKS CONSTRUCTIVE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH IPB SAYS NOMURA TALKS CONSTRUCTIVE.

text.p: Talks on Thursday between senior officals of the Czech bank IPB a.s. and Nomura over the Japanese investment bank's possible purchase of an equity stake in IPB were constructive, IPB said.

"(The talks) can be characterised as a continuation of a constructive dialogue over the posibilities of capital entry of this renowned world financial instiution in IPB," the Czech bank said in a brief statement after the meeting.
It said the talks would continue "on the level of the government and the Czech National Bank which in this issue are competent."

A central bank plan recently submitted to cabinet calls for the quick privatisation of the state's 31.7 percent in IPB, a suggestion already endorsed by the Finance Ministry earlier this month. The government, however, must approve any sale.
Nomura and Dutch ING NV are widely seen as potential partners for IPB.

The Czech daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Thursday quoted IPB General Director Jiri Tesar as saying both have indeed expressed an interest in buying the stake, currently held by the state agency the National Property Fund.
Tesar added that while he thinks Nomura would be satisified with acquiring the state's share, ING would probably want a majority stake in the bank.
